purpose: Structured, mechanically-discoverable registry of 'GOVERNANCE FLAG'-style callouts raised inline in claims.yaml prose (what_would_answer / evidence_quality_note / digestion_note) or in WORKSPACE_STATE.md Recent Work, most often by /thought-digestion sessions honouring the standing rule 'flag for /governance review, do not promote or resolve yourself mid-digestion'. Before this file existed, such flags were discoverable only by a human or agent noticing distinctive wording while reading a long, ever-growing WORKSPACE_STATE.md during /governance's own Session Startup Protocol orientation step -- which works only if the flag is recent enough to still be near the top. Confirmed staleness this caused: the ARC-033 promotion flag (GFLAG-0001, raised 2026-08-06) was still unactioned a full day later; the SD-014 discrepancy flag (GFLAG-0003, raised 2026-08-06) had already been resolved by an experiment run on 2026-08-04 that a LATER session had to independently re-discover from scratch because nothing pointed it at the open flag.
authority: This file is a derive-only, human/agent-adjudicated INPUT, exactly like sibling evidence/planning/*.v1.json files (see hypothesis_space_registry.v1.json's own authority note for the pattern). It never mutates claims.yaml, closure weights, or claim status by itself -- raising or resolving a flag here is bookkeeping, not a governance decision. /governance's own interactive review (see .claude/skills/governance/SKILL.md) is where a flag's substance actually gets acted on; this registry only guarantees the flag surfaces there instead of depending on luck.

flag_type_notes.promotion_review: A claim's status looks ready to move (e.g. candidate -> provisional/stable) but the flagging session deliberately did not promote it -- promotion is /governance's call, not a digestion-pass call.
flag_type_notes.evidence_discrepancy: A numeric, terminological, or structural mismatch was noticed (e.g. a claim describing N components when the substrate or a sibling claim implies a different N) that needs reconciliation, not just a note.
flag_type_notes.stale_note: A prose note (evidence_quality_note, live_status pointer, etc.) is suspected or confirmed to be pointing at outdated evidence and needs a governance-reviewed refresh.
flag_type_notes.contested_disposition: Two sessions, or a session and the user, reached different conclusions about how a claim should be classified or routed, and the disagreement was not resolved inline.

items.summary: The confirmed 2026-08-05 autopsy (V3-EXQ-867b section 2) records the screen-soundness violation as 'direct evidence the ON-arm manipulation itself perturbs whether/when decomposition fires', and that inference is carried verbatim into claims.yaml MECH-321 evidence_quality_note + what_would_answer and into hypothesis_space_registry observation_bottleneck + resolution.basis; 867b's own manifest contradicts it -- the violation appears in the OFF arm where the manipulation is provably inert (decomp_n_harm_bias_nonzero == 0 on every OFF cell), OFF-arm multi_action_commits DECREASED from the 4-episode screen to the 12-episode measurement on 5 seeds (impossible for a monotone counter over a prefix extension), and at full schedule the matching held perfectly (on_only and off_only tiers both EMPTY). ARC-004 FAILS its own registered what_would_answer, measured 2026-08-26. First execution of that falsifier -- its own text records the claim 'has never been tested as its own claim (absent from claim_evidence.v1.json) -- it is currently assumed via 36 dependents architecture, not measured'. PASS requires half-life(z_delta) > half-life(z_theta) > half-life(z_beta) by >= 0.8 SD of the seed-to-seed delta. Measured at 3 operating points, 5 seeds each (distinct stack init AND input stream), 1500 ticks: synthetic AR(1) rho=0.5 -> 1/5 seeds, margin +0.043 vs bar 0.060; rho=0.95 -> 1/5 seeds, margin +0.041 vs bar 0.653; REAL CausalGridWorld rollout -> 0/5 seeds, margin -0.159 vs bar 0.142, i.e. INVERTED (z_delta persists SHORTER than z_beta on every seed). Mechanism is transparent and read from source: alpha_shared=0.3 is a bare hardcoded literal applied identically to all three depths (stack.py:1454; note alpha_self/alpha_world ARE configurable, alpha_shared is not), and the beta->theta->delta cascade is a chain of UNTRAINED static projections (MECH-523), which change values but not temporal correlation -- so each depth inherits its input timescale under one identical EMA. White-noise control confirms: at rho=0 all three measure 1.89-1.91 against the EMA-alone prediction ln(0.5)/ln(0.7)=1.94. ARC-004's own FAIL branch prescribes the consequence: layers differ in content, not timescale; 'multi-timescale' is the wrong description of why they work; supersession review of the framing, structurally analogous to MECH-058 (asserted timescale separation for z_self/z_world, tested by lag-k autocorrelation in V3-EXQ-019, FAILED, retired, superseded by MECH-069 'incommensurable domains'). NO STATUS CHANGED HERE -- ARC-004 is active/standard with 36 dependents and this is governance's call. LIMITS, stated: encoders untrained (the as-built condition per MECH-523, and the condition ARC-004's own precondition frames, but a trained stack is untested); random-action policy on the real rollout; the 210-dim observation was split in half for body/world rather than using canonical channel routing, which should be redone before any supersession decision; the optional MECH-423 per-layer convergence corroboration was not run. items.summary: RESIDUAL of GFLAG-0106 (read that one first; it is resolved). Governance re-derived v4_spec's V3 full-completion gate on 2026-09-01 into MECH-477 + MECH-478 + MECH-479, and the user explicitly RETAINED MECH-479 in the V3 gate against the GOV-V4CUT-1 audit's proposal to move it to V4-phase validation. MECH-479 nevertheless still carries implementation_phase: v4, and the audit's stated ground for moving it was that testing prosocial_planning_requires_planned_system structurally requires V4-1 (others-as-slots, ARC-083). So the gate is now coherent in intent but inconsistent in labelling: a V3 completion gate names a v4-phase claim whose test has a v4 precondition. DECISION OWED, one of two: (i) let MECH-479's implementation_phase follow the dependency to v3 -- consistent with the standing rule that phase label follows dependency, and with the user's own reasoning that a V3 gate does not shed a hard leg; or (ii) re-derive the V4-1 precondition so the prosocial-planning leg is testable in V3 without others-as-slots, e.g. against a scripted or degenerate second agent. Do NOT resolve this by reverting to the old 'MECH-163 validated' wording -- that was unsatisfiable for a worse reason (it named a claim whose legs had been split out to MECH-478/479). Note the interaction with the still-open GFLAG-0105: the user's reading there is that MECH-274/276/278/ARC-031 may likewise be v3 prerequisites rather than V4, so option (i) may be one instance of a broader correction rather than a one-off.

HELD RESIDUAL of the MECH-317 partial-absorption disposition applied 2026-09-01 (REE_assembly 970117ca29; memo docs/architecture/mech_317_absorption_check.md; parents GFLAG-0066 and GFLAG-0087, both now resolved -- read 0087's resolution for why this was split out). ONE QUESTION, DELIBERATELY NOT ANSWERED BY THAT PASS: should MECH-318's and MECH-312b's depends_on edges to MECH-317 move to the ARC-071/MECH-323/MECH-324 cluster, or stay? The case for staying, which is why the pass declined to act: verdict (B) was PARTIAL absorption, so MECH-317 SURVIVES (narrowed to the action-stream boundary-readout claim, epistemic_category now substrate_conditional). A surviving claim's inbound edges are not automatically stale, and GFLAG-0087's 'repoint both' recommendation was written against the FULL supersede that was subsequently refused on the evidence tree -- so acting on it now would be applying a remedy for a disposition that did not happen. The case for moving: what MECH-318 and MECH-312b actually consume from MECH-317 is the COMPRESSION MECHANISM (MECH-318 abstracts the rule state under which the compressed options are deployed; MECH-312b weights arbitration by practice maturity over them), and that mechanism has moved -- it now lives in ARC-071/MECH-323/MECH-324. Post-narrowing, MECH-317 carries only the DV. So both consumers may now be pointing at a claim that no longer asserts the thing they depend on. VERIFIED FACTS EITHER WAY: no ARC-071-family claim mentions rule-state abstraction or practice-maturity weighting anywhere in its record, so a naive repoint would create edges into claims that assert neither; and MECH-312b is absent from GFLAG-0066's and GFLAG-0087's claim_ids entirely, so any disposition applied from those flags' claim lists alone would have orphaned it silently -- it is named here so that cannot recur. A third option exists and may be the right one: SPLIT the edge, pointing the mechanism dependency at the ARC-071 cluster while retaining a DV dependency on MECH-317 where the consumer genuinely needs the boundary readout. Decidable at a desk from the three consumers' own text; needs no run.

RESIDUAL of GFLAG-0105 (read that one first; it is resolved). ARC-059's own depends_on list spans all 3 developmental stages it names (self-as-object, objects-as-patterns, others-as-special-objects) including MECH-274 and MECH-278, both just relabeled implementation_phase: v4 with phase_locked: true because their own content genuinely needs V4 substrate (MECH-274: multi-agent modelling, zero substrate exists; MECH-278: object-schema-via-intervention, explicitly BYPASSED in V3 per object_representation_v4_plan.md). check_claim_phase_consistency.py now correctly reports these as CONFLICT (ARC-059 -> MECH-274, ARC-059 -> MECH-278) instead of silently re-deriving v3 on MECH-274/278. ARC-059 itself (implementation_phase: v3, v3_pending: true) is a claim ABOUT the ordering across all 3 stages -- its own scope may be over-broad for a single v3 label, since stage 3 (others-as-special-objects) is structurally V4 territory (needs another agent to exist). DECISION OWED: either (a) SPLIT ARC-059 per the F1-F4 pattern (minimal v3 form = stages 1-2 ordering only, self-as-object -> objects-as-patterns; v4 form = the full 3-stage claim including others), routing to /claim-synthesis, or (b) sever/retype the ARC-059->MECH-274 and ARC-059->MECH-278 depends_on edges if ARC-059's own v3-testable content genuinely does not need those specific specializations built. SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT surfaced in the same pass: MECH-276<->MECH-278 is a reciprocal depends_on cycle -- MECH-276's depends_on list includes MECH-278 (commented '# stage-2 specialisation'), which is backwards; MECH-278 already correctly lists MECH-276 as ITS dependency (the general principle a specialization depends on). check_claim_phase_consistency.py now flags this as a LOAD-BEARING cycle since MECH-276 stayed v3 (real substrate confirmed, GFLAG-0105) while MECH-278 moved to v4. Not fixed here (adjacent to but outside GFLAG-0105's exact 4-claim scope) -- the erroneous edge in MECH-276's depends_on should simply be deleted.

CROSS-REFERENCE for GFLAG-0109 (still open) -- read that one first. GFLAG-0109 speculated the user's GFLAG-0105 reading ('MECH-274/276/278/ARC-031 may likewise be v3 prerequisites rather than V4') might mean phase labels have drifted from dependencies GENERALLY, i.e. option (i) there (let MECH-479 follow dependency to v3) could be one instance of a broader pattern. GFLAG-0105 is now resolved and the answer is NOT a uniform pattern: 3 of 4 claims (MECH-274, MECH-278, ARC-031) were confirmed genuinely V4 (relabeled, phase_locked) -- their v3 labels were mechanical/stale, not independently-assessed drift toward v4 dependency. Only 1 of 4 (MECH-276) was genuinely mislabeled the OTHER direction: it should have stayed/is correctly v3, because real V3 substrate for it landed 2026-06-23 (ree_core/attribution/scientist_attribution_buffer.py) that the v4_spec.md cohort table never got updated to reflect. So the lesson for MECH-479 is narrower than 'apply option (i) broadly': check MECH-479's OWN substrate/dependency reality specifically (does real V3-tractable substrate for its prosocial-planning leg exist independent of ARC-083 others-as-slots, the way MECH-276 found an existing single-agent path?) rather than treating GFLAG-0105's outcome as a precedent that phase-follows-dependency always resolves toward v3. Full per-claim evidence in GFLAG-0105's resolution_note and the new GFLAG-0112 (ARC-059 depends_on breadth, out-of-scope follow-on).

Raise new entries and resolve existing ones only via scripts/governance_flag.py (raise / resolve subcommands), which commits via scripts/ree_commit.py in the same step -- this file lives under evidence/planning/, one of CLAUDE.md's exposed high-contention files, and a hand-edited whole-file read-modify-write here would silently adopt any other session's uncommitted edit (see CLAUDE.md 'Read-modify-write contamination'). /governance reads open items at the start of every cycle (see .claude/skills/governance/SKILL.md); the read is additive/informational only and never auto-resolves or auto-promotes anything -- governance is interactive and a flag's substance is always the user's call.
